The GP Coverage and Sourcing team within the Alternative Investment Platform is seeking an associate focused on growth and venture to join their team in New York City.

Our advisor-led wealth management businesses provide financial planning, investment management, banking and comprehensive advice to a wide range of clients, including ultra-high net worth and high net worth individuals, as well as family offices, foundations and endowments, and corporations and their employees. Alternative Investment Platform

GP Coverage and Sourcing

Within AIP, GP Coverage and Sourcing is responsible for leading the origination of alternative investment opportunities for GS Wealth clients. The venture and growth team team focuses on identifying and creating investment strategies including co-investments that meet client demand and address market opportunities by establishing and maintaining relationships with top tier managers. In addition, the team leads the structuring, capital markets and ongoing investor relations for each offering.

###HEADING###HOW YOU WILL FULFILL YOUR POTENTIAL

  • Deep understanding of financial markets and investment instruments 
  • 3+ year’s experience in wealth management, asset management, investment banking, or private equity
  • Strong quantitative, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Team player, with excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Sophisticated and tactful client manager who can effectively manage the entire investor lifecycle

Salary Range

About Us

Venice is the world’s leading consumer AI company built on principles of privacy, free speech, and user sovereignty. 

We’re building the Port City of AI, in which millions of individuals and AI agents gather, interact, and access sophisticated AI resources on a private and permissive foundation.  

Joining Venice means joining a team of unorthodox builders who believe in moving quickly, delivering a beautiful mass-market consumer product that doesn’t spy on people or censor their ideas and questions., If you’re energized by big ideas, entrepreneurial spirit, individual empowerment, and the opportunity to help shape a fast-growing company in the world’s hottest industry from the ground up, please reach out.

Why We’re Hiring

Venice is growing fast! Every day we are shipping new products, expanding into new modalities, and signing the agreements that make that possible: model and compute deals, vendor and SaaS paper, creator and marketing agreements, partnerships and NDAs.

Venice is a privacy-first company, which means we deliberately collect less user data than most companies in our space. We don’t track what we don’t need and we don’t store what we shouldn’t. This is a core part of who we are, and it’s not negotiable. Our contracts have to hold that line too, especially on data processing, retention and confidentiality.

Today, Venice’s in-house Office of General Counsel consists of one attorney, supported by external legal counsel as needed. With approximately 370 contract records across more than 200 counterparties and new agreements added nearly every business day, we are looking for a Senior Paralegal to take ownership of the contract lifecycle, from intake and review through execution, tracking, and renewal. This role will help our business teams move faster, improve consistency and efficiency across legal operations, and free up the General Counsel to focus on matters requiring attorney-level expertise.

This role reports to the General Counsel and works closely with business development and partnerships, finance, people operations, engineering, and the leadership team.

What You’ll Do

As the senior contracts paralegal at Venice.ai, you will support the commercial contract function of the Company’s (small but mighty) in-house Legal Department. Your work will touch upon the full contract lifecycle, from intake to drafting through negotiation, execution, monitoring, and periodic auditing of contracts. Some corporate maintenance responsibilities also fall within the scope of this role.

Primary responsibilities and duties include the following, listed in order of impact. You will work under the General Counsel’s supervision, inside approved playbooks and positions, and escalate anything outside them.

  • Run contract intake and first-pass review: Own contract intake and first-pass review. Run the legal intake queue, triage incoming requests, set due dates, and keep requesters informed (acknowledging each request within one business day). Review NDAs, vendor and SaaS order forms, MSAs, DPAs, creator and marketing agreements, and counterparty paper against Venice playbooks, and prepare issues lists and redlines within approved fallback positions.Draft and negotiate. Turn approved templates into finished agreements — website terms, privacy policies, talent releases, manufacturing and technology services agreements, professional services and influencer agreements — and run redline turns and follow-ups with counterparties. Website terms and privacy policies go to the General Counsel before use.
  • Own the contract catalog and the lifecycle. Confirm signer authority against the delegation-of-authority matrix, obtain fully executed copies, file them, and abstract key terms — term, renewal, notice, fees, governing law, liability, data — into the catalog. Audit the existing book for expiration, auto-renewal, and unfavorable terms, and run a renewal and notice calendar that gives business owners 90, 60, and 30 days' warning before each deadline.
  • Clear vendor security and privacy questionnaires from an approved answer library, working with Venice engineers, and maintain the record of each model provider's data-retention commitments. Flag anything the library doesn't cover.
  • Build the playbooks and templates. Help the General Counsel finish the NDA playbook and build the vendor/SaaS, DPA, creator and marketing, and consulting playbooks. Keep the template and clause library current, maintain the guidance on who can sign and how to get a contract reviewed, and track cycle times by contract type.
  • Support the Corporate Secretary. Prepare board and stockholder consents from approved forms, assemble and track signature packets, keep the minute book, officer and director records, secretary's certificates, and authority matrix current, and reconcile equity records with Carta and outside counsel. Handle routine entity maintenance and compliance filings.
  • Manage outside counsel and legal spend. Keep a matter list and engagement letters on file, review invoices against engagement terms and rates before approval, and report monthly spend by firm and matter against budget.
  • Keep compliance and IP deadlines on schedule. Maintain the legal team's compliance trackers, docket trademark and regulatory deadlines, inventory open-source licenses in use, and track insurance renewals.

*We retain the right to change or assign other duties to this position.

Who You Are

Required

  • 5+ years of experience in commercial contracting, including time in-house at a technology, SaaS, AI, fintech or crypto company.
  • Significant experience drafting, revising, and proofreading routine and commercial contracts. Additionally, you are comfortable with NDAs, SaaS and vendor agreements, order forms, MSAs and DPAs. 
  • Corporate secretary or entity management experience: minutes, board and stockholder consents and cap table records.
  • Proficiency with contract-management tools, Microsoft Office (including strong Word redlining skills), and Google Docs, plus hands-on experience with DocuSign or similar e-signature tools and with building or running a contract repository. Notion experience is a plus.
  • Extensive experience using AI in daily work to improve productivity, enhance accuracy, and streamline contract review and drafting, with the habit of checking their output.
  • Ability to work independently and efficiently with minimal supervision, and exercise sound judgment, including about what you can handle and what needs a lawyer.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, time management skills, multitasking skills, and above all, high agency
  • Discretion with privileged and confidential material, and clear, direct writing for counterparties and internal teams.

Preferred

  • Paralegal certificates or registrations from NALA or NFPA (such as the CP or RP credential).
  • Experience with data-processing, privacy and data-retention terms, and with AI model, compute or cloud agreements.
  • Experience with Carta or another equity management platform, and with Wyoming corporate records.
  • Experience reviewing law firm invoices and tracking legal spend.

You respect the privacy mission. You understand why Venice collects less data than competitors, and you want contracts that protect it.

You move fast and finish things. You would rather get a clean NDA out today than a perfect process next month, and you build the process as you go.

Team Description

The Trust team helps protect and strengthen confidence in Chainalysis by improving the security, compliance, and resilience of our products, services, and operations. We partner across Information Security, Procurement, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, and business teams to identify risk, make controls practical, and support responsible growth. Our work turns security expectations into clear, consistent processes that teams can use throughout the lifecycle of a business relationship.

Role Description

As the Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Analyst, you’ll own the day-to-day operation and continued improvement of Chainalysis’s third-party risk program. You’ll coordinate risk-based reviews of prospective and existing vendors, assess the evidence supporting their security practices, and help stakeholders understand and address material risks. You’ll also maintain the processes, records, and reporting that make third-party risk visible and manageable from intake through renewal and off-boarding.

This is a hands-on, cross-functional role for someone who can bring structure to a growing vendor portfolio, exercise sound judgment, and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical partners.

In this role, you’ll

  • Own the third-party risk review lifecycle, coordinating intake, risk categorization and tiering, due diligence, ongoing monitoring, reassessment, and offboarding.

  • Integrate security and privacy risk checkpoints into procurement workflows, partnering with Procurement to ensure reviews begin early in vendor selection and are completed before onboarding or material changes to a service.

  • Review vendor security and privacy materials—including questionnaires, SOC reports, ISO certifications, penetration-test summaries, vulnerability-management information, and business continuity and disaster recovery documentation—and assess the supporting evidence for relevance and sufficiency.

  • Conduct risk-based assessments that consider the service being provided, the data involved, the vendor’s access, and the potential impact to Chainalysis; coordinate enhanced due diligence for higher-risk relationships.

  • Document assessment results, control gaps, residual risk, and practical recommendations in a way that business owners and control partners can understand and act on.

  • Work with vendor relationship owners and partners in Security, Procurement, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, and other business teams to resolve open questions, agree on mitigations, and escalate material or overdue risks.

  • Track findings and remediation commitments through closure, review remediation evidence, and coordinate risk exceptions or acceptance through the appropriate decision-makers.

  • Maintain accurate vendor risk records, assessment artifacts, and monitoring activities in the relevant program tools; help keep vendor inventory and risk status current.

  • Coordinate periodic reviews and reassessments, including when a vendor has a significant security incident, material service or data-use change, or other change in risk.

  • Develop clear program reporting on assessment status, vendor risk, findings, remediation aging, and exceptions; identify recurring issues and recommend improvements.

  • Improve assessment guidance, templates, and workflows to make the program more consistent and efficient while preserving appropriate risk oversight.

We’re looking for candidates who have

  • 6+ years of experience in cybersecurity, third-party risk management, information security, or GRC

  • 3+ years of direct experience conducting or managing vendor security or third-party risk assessments.

  • Experience reviewing and analyzing vendor assurance materials such as SOC 1/SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certifications, security questionnaires, penetration-test reports, and business continuity documentation.

  • A working understanding of security and privacy controls across areas such as cloud and SaaS security, access management, data protection, vulnerability management, incident response, and business continuity.

  • Familiarity with common control frameworks or assurance standards such as NIST, ISO 27001, and SOC 2.

  • The ability to distinguish documented, supportable evidence from unverified statements, identify meaningful gaps, and make proportionate, risk-based recommendations.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex risk clearly and diplomatically to varied audiences.

  • Experience coordinating work across multiple internal stakeholders and external vendors, with strong organization and follow-through on actions and deadlines.

  • Attention to detail and comfort working with structured records, assessment data, and program reporting.

Nice to have experience

  • Experience using a third-party risk management or GRC platform.

  • Experience with vendor security monitoring tools.

  • Familiarity with privacy assessments, subcontractor or fourth-party risk, and security requirements in vendor contracts.

  • Experience supporting a technology, SaaS, fintech, financial services, or other regulated organization.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

Abuse Control Engineering (ACE) is Stripe’s rapid-response technical defense and control incubator. When urgent abuse vectors emerge, ACE uses real-world attacker telemetry to prototype, test, and deploy software safeguards before vulnerabilities can be exploited at scale.

We partner closely with Fraud, Risk, Abuse Research, and Product Engineering to run rigorous experiments that balance effective risk mitigation with legitimate user activity and conversion. Operating as both a strike team and an incubator, ACE builds automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring and transfers mature controls to long-term product owners across Stripe.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Control Engineer on the ACE team, you will design, prototype, and incubate technical defenses that safeguard Stripe’s financial ecosystem against complex, cross-cutting abuse vectors.

When emerging threat patterns reveal weaknesses in Stripe products, ACE rapidly builds and experiments with technical safeguards. Guided by empirical evidence and Stripe’s Fraud Taxonomy 3.0 (FT3) framework, you will translate threat intelligence into precise technical control requirements, such as API rate limits, step-up challenges, parameter validation, and pre-debit holds.

You will run experiments to evaluate risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, carefully balancing security and product velocity. You will manage controls through a structured incubation lifecycle, build automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring, and partner with product engineering teams to transfer mature, long-term defenses.

Responsibilities

  • Rapid control prototyping: Design, prototype, and deploy technical controls across API, protocol, and product boundaries to address high-impact abuse vectors.
  • Evidence-based technical requirements: Translate empirical attacker evidence and FT3 threat research from Abuse Research, Fraud, and Security teams into precise technical abuse requirements and control specifications.
  • Control co-design: Collaborate with teams across Stripe to design resilient, secure controls across payments, onboarding, identity, and Connect surfaces.
  • Risk experimentation: Run rigorous experiments and A/B tests to measure risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, optimizing controls to minimize friction while neutralizing threats.
  • Regression testing: Build comprehensive regression test suites and automated attack simulations with Abuse Research to ensure mitigated abuse vectors do not recur.
  • Stakeholder management: Execute ACE’s incubation model by defining handoff criteria, operational documentation, timelines, and target dates for transferring successful controls to product teams.

Who you are

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in security engineering, software engineering, application security, or anti-abuse engineering in a high-scale production environment.
  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • A strong software development background, with proficiency in Python, Go, Java, or a similar production programming language, as well as advanced SQL skills for analyzing system telemetry.
  • Experience using frontier AI models for software development, learning, and analysis.
  • Hands-on experience building API-level safeguards, rate-limiting frameworks, authentication or authorization checks, or input-validation controls.
  • Experience with automated testing frameworks, including writing unit, integration, and regression tests for critical backend software.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with a track record of partnering across security, product, and platform teams to drive technical outcomes.

Preferred qualifications

  • A track record of designing and executing A/B tests, evaluating control efficacy, and balancing security safeguards against user conversion friction.
  • Expertise in threat modeling, secure systems architecture, and modern application-security design principles.
  • Familiarity with established threat frameworks, such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&CK, and experience applying adversary kill-chain analysis to build resilient defenses.
  • Knowledge of financial fraud vectors, threat-actor tactics, techniques, and procedures, and attacker infrastructure, including account takeover, card testing, and credential stuffing.
  • Hands-on experience with large-scale data-processing platforms, such as Databricks, Trino, or PySpark, to monitor and measure control performance across distributed systems.

About the company
 
Hi, we're Ondo Finance. Our mission is to provide institutional-grade, blockchain-enabled investment products and services. We have both a technology arm that develops decentralized finance technology, and an asset management arm that creates and manages tokenized funds. We are the global leader in tokenized treasuries, tokenized stocks and ETFs, and are building the future of institutional-grade financial services onchain.
 
Founded by folks from Goldman Sachs Digital Assets Team, we’re backed by some of the best investors in the world including Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Pantera Capital, Tiger Global, and more. We are currently the leaders in the space in terms of AUM and are well capitalized to continue growing the firm. We're fully remote, with team members across the U.S.
 
About the role

Ondo's user research team is small but mighty, and works horizontally across the whole product suite, not inside a single pod. We're hiring a senior quantitative user researcher to build and lead quantitative research across the portfolio.

You'll set your own UXR strategy with minimal guidance, take on the hardest decision-shaping questions whichever team they come from, and answer them with evidence that holds up at scale.

What You'll Do
  • Own the research intake and quant roadmap. Field research questions from product, design, GTM and leadership. Turn vague asks into answerable questions, decide which need quantitative evidence (and which don't), and prioritize where evidence most reduces risk on our biggest bets.
  • Answer the big questions before launch. Use MaxDiff and conjoint to show which features, benefits and messages actually drive decisions. Design pre-launch experiments (stimulus tests, matched cohorts, vignettes, threshold studies) with decision rules set before fielding, and pretest instruments with cognitive interviews.
  • Build measurement and segments that last. Adapt or develop validated scales for trust, perceived security and comprehension, track them across products and markets, and turn our user profiles into statistically validated, sized segments.
  • Get data you can trust, and connect it to behavior. Design sampling, translation and fraud controls for a global, crypto-native audience, and partner with data science to link survey data with product data.
  • Evaluate AI-assisted experiences. Design human evaluation for AI-assisted finance features: rubrics, rater reliability, and whether user trust matches how reliable the system actually is.
  • Be leadership's partner for evidence. Present findings as recommendations with effect sizes, confidence and what would change the call. Give quick, right-sized answers to ad-hoc leadership questions, whether that's existing data, a fast pulse survey or a full study. Set the standards that let PMs and designers run sound lightweight surveys or data-driven validation themselves.
Requirements
  • 7+ years of UX or applied research experience, including at least 5 years leading quantitative studies end to end, from study design through recommendation.
  • Experience leading quantitative research studies for financial products (e.g., brokerage, trading, banking, payments, wealth or lending).
  • A self-starter who operates with minimal guidance: you scope ambiguous problems, set your own priorities, and drive studies to a decision.
  • Deep survey science expertise: sampling and weighting, instrument design, bias control, data-quality screening, and programming in Qualtrics or similar.
  • Hands-on experience designing and analyzing MaxDiff and/or conjoint studies.
  • Strong applied statistics: regression, power analysis, and experimental and quasi-experimental design.
  • Fluency in R or Python for analysis and visualization.
  • You have an existing AI-assisted research setup, from drafting survey instruments to writing and reviewing analysis code, and you proofread/validate every output with rigor.
  • A track record of quantitative work that changed a product or business decision, and the ability to explain uncertainty clearly to executives and non-researchers.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with crypto, onchain or tokenized-asset products.
  • A master’s or PhD in a quantitative field such as statistics, survey methodology, behavioral economics, or marketing science.
  • Depth in advanced methods, such as hierarchical Bayes and simulators, psychometric scale development, segmentation, pricing research, or SQL and multilevel modeling.
  • Experience evaluating AI or LLM-powered products, such as human evaluation design, rubrics or rater reliability.
  • Research across markets in LATAM, APAC or EMEA, including translating survey instruments.
  • Responsible AI-native research workflows, such as using LLM tools to speed up instrument design, coding of open-ended responses or analysis.
What we offer
  • Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation.
  • Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO).
  • Remote-first team across many countries — You will be an early team member helping shape our vision, culture, and design practices.
  • A+ colleagues — Our team includes alumni from: Goldman Sachs, Blackrock, Two Sigma, Bridgewater, SpaceX, AWS, Meta, Google, McKinsey, Circle, Uniswap.
  • Best-in-class investors — We are proud to be backed by leading crypto experts and VCs, including Pantera Capital, Founders Fund and Coinbase Ventures.
